clues.title: Plate: black with yellow-red emblem
text: Liechtenstein uses black plates with white lettering and a yellow-and-red emblem near the left side. When blurred, the plates will appear grey, with the emblem colours being visible.
clues.summary: Black plates with white letters and a yellow-and-red emblem near the left. When blurred they look grey but the emblem colours still show.

clues.title: Landscape: flat valley, mountains to the east
text: Most coverage in Liechtenstein is situated in a somewhat flat river valley, but with tall mountains in almost every direction. In particular, within this valley, you will almost always be able to see the nearby mountains towering above you to the east. Most of the mountainous coverage is just on the slopes of the mountains, with only a small amount properly in the mountains.
As a result of the flat Rhine River Valley, Liechtenstein has a lot of pastures and other agricultural land.
clues.summary: Most coverage is in a flat river valley with tall mountains almost everywhere, always towering to the east. Pastures and farmland fill the valley floor.

clues.title: Google car: low camera, big car blur
text: All coverage in Liechtenstein is **low-cam**. This means that the camera on the Google car is intentionally set up lower than in most other countries. This can be recognized in two ways:
- The car blur is significantly bigger.
- Roads look wider and objects around you are seen from a lower angle.
Generally, the bigger car blur is the most consistent way to recognize low-cam.

NOTE: The only other countries that always have low-cam are [Switzerland](https://maps.app.goo.gl/mq5nCexiy7KfsV8E8) and [Japan](https://www.google.com/maps/@35.8415638,139.9145236,3a,75y,305.11h,83.84t/data=!3m7!1e1!3m5!1sLyYnyrI7fgLeL5Ev09XeJg!2e0!6shttps:%2F%2Fstreetviewpixels-pa.googleapis.com%2Fv1%2Fthumbnail%3Fpanoid%3DLyYnyrI7fgLeL5Ev09XeJg%26cb_client%3Dmaps_sv.tactile.gps%26w%3D203%26h%3D100%26yaw%3D33.088177%26pitch%3D0%26thumbfov%3D100!7i16384!8i8192).
clues.summary: The camera sits lower than usual, so the car blur is much bigger and roads look wider. The big blur is the easiest sign. Switzerland and Japan also always have it.

clues.title: Bollard: black-white cylinder, blue side tab
text: Liechtenstein uses **black-and-white **cylindrical bollards** **with a white or grey reflector and a rounded top. They also often have a blue attachment on the side.
When attached to guardrails, they will use the [wedge design](https://maps.app.goo.gl/zDoFQvaitWHeGPhk9) instead.
NOTE: Switzerland can use almost identical bollards.
clues.summary: A black-and-white cylinder with a rounded top, white or grey reflector, and often a blue attachment on the side. On guardrails it uses a wedge shape instead. Swiss bollards can look almost identical.

clues.title: Sign: green-white bus stop, LIEMOBIL
text: Bus stops in Liechtenstein use a **green-and-white** design, with a black metallic border around the sign. The phrase LIEMOBIL is written at the top.
NOTE: The metallic frame is not always black.
clues.summary: Green-and-white bus stop sign with a black metal border and LIEMOBIL written at the top. The frame is not always black.

clues.title: Direction sign: white or blue, pointed arrow
text: Like Switzerland, directional signs in Liechtenstein are generally white (smaller roads) or blue (bigger roads), and they have a pointed arrowhead, with a contrasting colour.
clues.summary: Direction signs are white on small roads and blue on bigger ones, with a pointed arrowhead in a contrasting colour. Same as Switzerland.

clues.title: Pedestrian sign: seven stripes, tall rectangle
text: Liechtenstein pedestrian signs have **seven stripes**. The signs also have an oddly tall rectangle.
NOTE: Switzerland uses identical signs.
clues.summary: Seven zebra stripes inside an oddly tall rectangle. Switzerland uses identical signs.

clues.title: Road separator: yellow-black, Lego-like knob
text: You can find these** yellow-and-black** **striped **road separators, with a **rounded top**, and a **Lego-like knob** on the top. They have 3 stripes of both colours, with yellow on the bottom.
NOTE: Switzerland uses a variety of different Road Separators, some of which will look identical to the ones in Liechtenstein.
clues.summary: Yellow-and-black striped road separators with a rounded top and a knob on top: 3 stripes of each colour, yellow at the bottom. Some Swiss separators look identical.

clues.title: Sign: round grey metal border
text: Road signs in Liechtenstein commonly have a round, grey **metal border** around them.
NOTE: Swiss and German signs can also have similar metallic borders.
clues.summary: Road signs often have a round grey metal border. Swiss and German signs can have similar borders.

clues.title: Houses: Alpine mix of old and modern
text: Architecture in Liechtenstein is a blend of traditional Alpine styles and more modern buildings, especially in the bigger cities.
clues.summary: A blend of traditional Alpine houses and more modern buildings, mostly in the larger towns.

clues.title: Landscape: dense mountain slope above valley
text: Triesenberg and its surroundings are a fairly densely populated area on the slope of the mountains just east of the Rhine River Valley, which can often be seen below to the west.
clues.summary: A fairly built-up area on a mountain slope, with the flat river valley often visible below to the west.

clues.title: Landscape: mountains all around
text: Mountains can be seen all around in the coverage east of the mountain ridge that cuts through Liechtenstein.
clues.summary: East of the main mountain ridge, mountains surround you in every direction.

clues.title: Landscape: small forested ridge to the south
text: Around Ruggell, there is a small, forested ridgeline to the south. This is a big contrast to the towering mountains seen elsewhere.
clues.summary: In the northwest corner, a small forested ridgeline lies to the south, a big contrast to the tall mountains elsewhere.

clues.title: Landscape: built-up ridge north, big mountains
text: Around Mauren, you can see the aforementioned ridge to the north, but this side of the hills is much more developed and urban. And to the south and southeast, you will see the much bigger mountains usually seen to the east.
clues.summary: In the north, you see a low ridge to the north with more buildings on its side, and much bigger mountains to the south and southeast.

clues.title: Landscape: rolling hills in the northeast
text: There is a set of **rolling hills** that run from Bendern, northeast, to the Austrian border. The rest of Liechtenstein is either very flat or in the mountains.
clues.summary: A band of rolling hills runs northeast toward the Austrian border. The rest of the country is either very flat or in the mountains.

clues.title: Landscape: two rocky peaks to the north
text: In the flat area west of Balzers, with the northeast-oriented gridded roads, to the North/Northwest, you can often see [two rocky peaks](https://maps.app.goo.gl/8ZpQjESH7z189v4g9) on the Swiss side.
clues.summary: In the flat southwest with a diagonal road grid, you can often see two rocky peaks to the north or northwest, across the border in Switzerland.

clues.title: Sign: red bus stop sign
text: Unlike the rest of Liechtenstein, Vaduz sometimes uses **red bus stop signs.**
NOTE: ** **Regular bus stops are also present.
clues.summary: In the capital, red bus stop signs sometimes appear. Normal ones are there too.

clues.title: Sign: black bus stop sign
text: Unlike the rest of Liechtenstein, Balzers sometimes uses **black bus stop signs.**
NOTE: ** **Regular bus stops are also present.
clues.summary: In the far south, black bus stop signs sometimes appear. Normal ones are there too.

clues.title: Street sign: blue with thin white border
text: Blue street signs with a thin white border will place you either in the south of Liechtenstein or in the north around Bandern.
clues.summary: Blue street signs with a thin white border mean the south or the north near Bendern.

clues.title: Street sign: blue with no outline
text: Blue street signs that don’t have an outline are found in Eschen.
clues.summary: Blue street signs without an outline are from one northern town.

clues.title: Street sign: flat black
text: Flat black signs are found in eastern Liechtenstein.
clues.summary: Flat black signs are found in the east.

clues.title: Street sign: black, white border, raised letters
text: Black signs with a white border and embossed letters can be found in Schaan.
clues.summary: Black signs with a white border and embossed letters are from one central town.

clues.title: Street sign: brown with old German-style font
text: These brown street signs with a font reminiscent of **traditional German typefaces**, along with a white border, are found in Vaduz and the northern towns.
clues.summary: Brown street signs with a white border and a font like traditional German lettering, in the capital and northern towns.

clues.title: Street sign: brown with arrow design
text: Brown street signs that have an **arrow design** are unique to Ruggell.
NOTE: The regular brown signs are also present in Ruggell.
clues.summary: Brown street signs shaped like an arrow are unique to one northern town, though regular brown signs appear there too.

clues.title: Street sign: brown, plain generic font
text: Browns signs which have a more ‘generic’ font will place you in Planken.
clues.summary: Brown signs with a plain, generic font belong to the small village of Planken.

clues.title: Landscape: steep rocky cliff with trees
text: This steep rocky cliff with trees at its base and on the top can be seen in and around Mäls.
clues.summary: A steep rocky cliff with trees at its base and on top, seen near the village of Mäls.

clues.title: Landscape: the only lakes
text: The only lakes in Liechtenstein are located just south of Steg, near the middle of the mountains.
clues.summary: The only lakes in the country are just south of Steg, in the middle of the mountains.
